objective: Under G18, at the coordinator's pick with the owner's idea of 'a sign to the sides' in a complex meeting pattern: on meeting patterns made by ordinary growth that have a symmetry exchanging two sides, with no added rule, (1) do the allowed states sort into those the swap keeps and those it turns into their complement, and does the pattern carry a two-valued label from it; (2) is there a pattern where going round a loop returns with the sides exchanged, so that the label cannot be removed by relabelling; (3) can such a label weight whole configurations so that two completions of one reading cancel, with readers' settings free and no signalling? Stop at a native sign with a frozen runnable test, or at an argument or clean census showing every such label is trivial or supplied by us.
status: Complete 2026-11-26 (obstruction learned; a census with arguments; referee pending): swaps of two sides are made and kept by growth and one-sided swaps carry a twist no renaming removes, but its only trace in the states is the kept/flipped sort, which weighs nothing; with values read no sign acts; under readings that sum signed completions the swap's signs reach the PR box, but random pairings and single-distinction signs do as well, so the excess is the reading's.
title: A sign to the sides: does a swap of two sides of a meeting pattern make a sign?
